---
title: Change, rename or delete a type
sidebar_label: Change or delete a type
headTitle: Change, rename or delete a type, step by step
description: Check a change to a registered type, replace its definition, move its items to another type to rename it, and delete a type nothing uses.
job: A builder changes, renames or deletes a type without losing items or breaking what names it.
kind: how-to
---

**Changing, renaming or deleting a type moves or removes its items,** so each step starts with a check. The examples change the receipt type from [Define a type](/build/define-a-type): each call sends `receipt.json`, and `definition` is that file read in. `marfa` in the TypeScript tabs is a client from [the TypeScript SDK](/reference/typescript-sdk#create-a-client), and `api` in the Swift tabs a `Client` from [the Swift SDK](/reference/swift-sdk/server-calls#the-api-client).

That guide's key can check a change and add an optional field. **Removing a field, making one required and deleting a type need `schema.write`,** which an app's everyday key shouldn't hold: make a key with `--permission schema.write` for those changes alone, and revoke it afterwards.

## Check the change

A replacement **sends the whole definition.** To add an optional category, add `"version": 1` and a `category` field of type `enum`, with its `enum_values`, to `receipt.json`. Normalizing shows what would change and changes nothing, and any key can do it:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa types normalize --file receipt.json
```

```http tab="HTTP"
POST /types/normalize
Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY
Content-Type: application/json

<the contents of receipt.json>
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const { data, error } = await marfa.POST("/types/normalize", { body: definition });
```

```swift tab="Swift"
let normalized = try await api.check(itemType: definition)
```

The answer's `type` is your definition with its defaults written out, and `registered_type` the registered one in the same form, `null` if there is none. Compare those two, not `resolved_type`, which adds inherited fields.

## Replace the type

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa types replace app.example.receipt --file receipt.json
```

```http tab="HTTP"
PUT /types/app.example.receipt
Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY
Content-Type: application/json

<the contents of receipt.json>
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const { data, error } = await marfa.PUT("/types/{id}", {
  params: { path: { id: "app.example.receipt" } },
  body: definition,
});
```

```swift tab="Swift"
import Foundation
import MarfaAPI

let update = try JSONDecoder().decode(
    Components.Schemas.TypeDefinitionUpdate.self, from: Data(contentsOf: receiptURL))
_ = try await api.replace(itemType: "app.example.receipt", with: update)
```

**Send the `version` every time:** a replacement without one sets it back to 0. A type Marfa ships can't be replaced or deleted: `403 core_type_immutable`.

**A replacement changes no item you already hold.** A property you made required is checked the next time an item's properties are written, a property you removed leaves the items' values in place, and a rule you tightened refuses only a write that changes that property. A change to `title_field` or `body_field` changes how items are [named and previewed](/catalog/display-hints#names-and-previews).

A type can't reshape a field it inherits: `400 inheritance_violation`. **A new Marfa release can still leave a clash,** by giving a built-in type a field your type declares in another shape. Your type keeps working, and `marfa types list --json` gives it a `conflicts` list: declare the field as `inherited` says, or leave it out.

## Rename a type by moving its items

**A type's identifier never changes.** To rename a type, or fold one into another, register the new type, move the items to it, then delete the old type. Each item keeps its ID, edges, tags and files. The examples move `app.example.receipt` to `app.example.expense`, which requires a `paid` property.

**Preview first** with `--dry-run`, or `dry_run: true` over HTTP. It changes nothing and lists the items it would move, the settings that name the type, and the keys and apps whose type map names it. A move takes every item of exactly that type your key can see, in any state; an item in the bin stays there.

**Marfa checks each item against the new type,** as it checks any write. To add a property the new type requires, send it in `properties`, merged into every item:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa types move app.example.receipt app.example.expense --properties '{"paid":false}'
```

```http tab="HTTP"
POST /types/app.example.receipt/move
Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY
Content-Type: application/json

{ "to": "app.example.expense", "properties": { "paid": false } }
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const { data: job, error } = await marfa.POST("/types/{id}/move", {
  params: { path: { id: "app.example.receipt" } },
  body: { to: "app.example.expense", properties: { paid: false } },
});
```

```swift tab="Swift"
import Marfa // the JSON values in `properties`
import MarfaAPI

let started = try await api.startMove(ofType: "app.example.receipt", to: "app.example.expense", properties: ["paid": false])
let job = try await api.follow(moveJob: started.id)
```

Over HTTP, Marfa answers `202` with a [bulk-action job](/reference/api/bulk-actions/getBulkActionJob) to read until it is `completed`. The CLI and Swift's `follow(moveJob:)` wait. An agent previews and confirms the move in two calls of `marfa_move_items`. Each moved item sends an `item.updated` [event](/build/events).

**An item the new type refuses stays where it is.** Without `properties`, the CLI says which and exits `1`:

<Terminal>

```bash
marfa types move app.example.receipt app.example.expense
```

```text
moved 0 of 2 items from app.example.receipt to app.example.expense
it couldn't move 2 items:
  01a1fc3b-36d3-74ad-bbfa-f682c179286f invalid_properties: Cannot move item to "app.example.expense": paid: Required field is missing
  01a1fc3b-36e3-7447-aa10-6469c0ad6d0f invalid_properties: Cannot move item to "app.example.expense": paid: Required field is missing
2 items you can see are still app.example.receipt
```

</Terminal>

The finished job's `result.remaining` counts the items of the old type your key can see, and `result.remaining_hidden` is `true` when one it can't see remains. Deal with them and run the move again.

**Once every item has moved, Marfa changes the folders, views and webhooks that name the old type** to name the new one: a folder's `query.types`, `defaults.type` and `first_placement`, a view's `query.types`, each `type eq` or `type neq` filter term, and a webhook's `type_filter` when it is exactly the type. A folder keeps its files where they are. While any item of the old type remains, Marfa changes no setting. A move never changes a key's or an app's type map: [give them](/run/manage-keys) the new type before you delete the old one.

Marfa refuses a move with `409 type_move_blocked`, naming each setting and a `reason`, when it can't rewrite a setting: a `filter_term` such as `type starts_with "acme.d"`, a folder's `placement_conflict`, a webhook on a type with `subtypes`, or one your key can't change, `not_permitted`. Change that setting, then move again. A move needs write on both types and on each setting, and only the key or app that made a webhook, with `webhooks.manage`, can change it.

## Delete a type

Marfa deletes a type that **no item holds,** in any state, the bin included, that no folder, view, webhook or [table](/build/tables) column names, and that no type names as its parent or in `compatible_with`:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa types delete app.example.receipt
```

```http tab="HTTP"
DELETE /types/app.example.receipt
Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
await marfa.DELETE("/types/{id}", {
  params: { path: { id: "app.example.receipt" } },
});
```

```swift tab="Swift"
try await api.delete(itemType: "app.example.receipt")
```

Otherwise Marfa refuses it: `409 type_has_subtypes` names the `subtype_ids`, `422 compatible_with_violation` the `dependent_type_ids`, and `409 type_in_use` the `item_count`, `settings` and `columns`. For `type_in_use`, move the items first.

<Callout type="warn" title="A forced delete blocks writes to the items">
`force=true` (the CLI's `--force`) deletes a type that items still hold or a setting names, though a subtype or a `compatible_with` claim still blocks it. The items stay, and are still read, listed and found, but a write of an item's properties, tier or time is refused `400 unknown_type` until the type is registered again. You can still tag them, archive them or move them to the bin.
</Callout>

The rules behind this guide are in the [types](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/types.md) chapter of the contract.
